question: Vacation, resignation and removal from the offices of Speaker and Deputy Speaker are addressed in which Article of the Constitution of India?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 94**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 94** of the **Indian Constitution** deals with the **vacation, resignation, and removal** from the offices of the **Speaker and Deputy Speaker** of the **House of the People (Lok Sabha).**
 
• According to this article, the **Speaker or Deputy Speaker** must vacate their office in the following cases:
 
 
• When they cease to be a member of the **House of the People**.
 
• When they resign from their position by submitting a letter to another presiding officer.
 
• When they are removed from office by a resolution passed by a majority of all the members of the **Lok Sabha**.
 
 
 
• The resolution for removal requires a **14-day notice** before being moved in the House.
 
• This article ensures the accountability and proper functioning of the offices of the **Speaker and Deputy Speaker** in India's parliamentary system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 70**__

 __
 
• **Article 70** of the **Indian Constitution** deals with the discharge of the functions of the **President** in certain contingencies.
 
• It empowers Parliament to make laws regarding how the functions of the President will be discharged in case of a vacancy in the office or if the President is unable to perform duties due to absence, illness, or any other reason.
 
 
 
• **Article 101**__
 __
 
• **Article 101** lays down provisions regarding the **vacation of seats**, disqualifications, and **dual membership** in the Parliament.
 
• It prevents a person from being a member of both Houses of Parliament at the same time and addresses conditions for vacating a seat.
 
 
 
• **Article 84**__
 
 
• **Article 84** specifies the **qualifications** required to be elected as a member of **Parliament**.
 
• These include being a citizen of India, meeting the minimum age requirement, and other criteria prescribed by law.
